B-CLOSE.note: main session; regenerated evidence only, no verdict or digest of an existing spec changes

B0.note: main session: must equal A0 except benchmark noise

BODY-CORE.note: specs re-authored for B-R7/B-R9 are edited by their owners (listed in the handoff); must merge together with NAV-M5

BODY-ENGINE.note: must merge together with NAV-M2 (--package BODY-ENGINE+NAV-M2)

CAM-RUNTIME.note: nothing may change in room mode

GEN.note: furnishers registered but returning at once for gen 1 are allowed (1.16)

K-EVAL.note: adoption-round kernel follow-ups (evaluation side): no verdict, digest or fingerprint may change (its gate runs on an isolated copy, `isolate --package K-EVAL`, against a pristine one)

K-GATE.note: phase-1 kernel agent: gate and process tooling; may write the policy files' format (the main session commits them)

K-GATE2.note: phase-1 red team, second gate pass: hand-over bases, perf job, never-acted wrong plans, golden policy

K-GATE3.note: phase-1 close-out, the gate tool: rules in committed policy, gate-code digests, protected scope, golden re-records signed, wall-clock bounds registered and run relaxed, the Python 3.9 lint

NAV-M2.note: navigation_robot domain agent, paired with BODY-ENGINE

P1-ALL.note: phase 1 of the stabilisation, merged (16 domains' fixes, kernel agents, K-GATE)

P1-FIX2.note: phase-1 red-team fix pass (non-domain files): kernel leaks, gate honesty, verifier interim rule, CI, tools

P1-INT.note: phase-1 kernel agents (K-FIX, K-LEAK) and the phase-1 integrator: kernel-side fixes and requests, re-records

P1C.note: the phase-1 close-out record (`record --id P1C --package P1C --prev P1F`): the six domains' files of the round, the gate tool's and the round's reports

P1C-INT.note: the close-out integrator's fixes in non-domain files (kernel, tasks, eval, generator, tools, kernel tests, docs, re-records); join it to the record with --package P1C+P1C-INT

P1C:admin_inventory.note: phase-1 close-out: admin_inventory's rows of finish_breakages.json

P2-S1.note: phase 2 stage 1 merged: WP1 (with the WP2 stub) WP2 WP3 WP4 WP7 WP9 WP11 (budget 1.15 for WP2's attribution overhead)

P2-S3.note: phase 2 stage 3 merged: WP6 and the 16 WP-D packages

P2-S6.note: phase 2 stage 6: fixes after R0 and the exit tests (23.6) in non-domain files: every file of WP1-WP11 (domain fixes go through the WP-D packages)

P2-WP1.note: WP1 LEDGER (with the WP2 stub): no schema 2/3 verification outcome may change (section 25)

P2-WP10.note: WP10 REVIEW, AUDIT, GATE, SPLITS, HARNESS: the gate's new stages (its own test and README added to section 25's list); a record made by its uncommitted gate script needs a gate-change signature

P2-WP11.note: WP11 CORE SKILLS: fixes world behaviour (P10), may change legacy outcomes; lists every legacy spec whose outcome changes and fixes or flags it (section 25)

P2-WP2.note: WP2 ATTRIBUTION, FLOWS, FINISH: logs.gone / logs.mess_flows change state digests (and the room golden, re-recorded with signed golden rows); attribution overhead at most 15 % of simulation time (6.2), hence the G7 budget 1.15 x prev

P2-WP3.note: WP3 TIMING: no schema 2/3 verification outcome may change

P2-WP4.note: WP4 CONTENT: no verdict may change; core's flow logging writes WP2's logs (state digests, the golden)

P2-WP5.note: WP5 VERIFY CORE: 14.3 rule 1 and the schema-4 build change legacy verdicts (each reviewed and signed)

P2-WP6.note: WP6 BATTERY: new files only; no outcome may change

P2-WP7.note: WP7 PERCEPTION EVIDENCE: no schema 2/3 verification outcome may change

P2-WP8.note: WP8 SCHEMA 4 + LINTS: specs stay schema 2/3, so no outcome may change

P2-WP9.note: WP9 SETUP RANDOMISATION: the new ops and the seeded placement permutation are schema 4 only (9.2), so no legacy house, digest or verdict may change
